source.paraphrase: The source regularizes f by delta/2 times squared distance from x0, calls a strongly convex solver to error epsilon/2, and chooses delta=epsilon/R². Comparison with a supplied minimizer of f transfers error and bounds the regularized minimizer radius. The remaining proof uses smoothness beta+delta and a small-accuracy regime to control condition number and oracle complexity.
source.scope: The proposed theorem closes existence and finite comparison/error ingredients only. Smoothness/strong convexity of W, solver realization, query cost and full Lemma4.2 remain distinct.

mathematical_assessment.assumptions: Positive R,epsilon; delta=epsilon/R²>0; continuous real-valued f on a proper normed space, supplied global minimizer z and norm(z-x0)<=R. No differentiability/convexity/smoothness is needed for this finite component.
mathematical_assessment.existence: W is continuous. Compact closedBall(x0,R) is nonempty and contains z. Minimize W there. Outside the ball, norm(y-x0)>R>=norm(z-x0) and f(y)>=f(z), so positive penalty implies W(y)>W(z). The compact minimizer has W(w)<=W(z), hence is a global minimizer, not only a constrained-ball minimizer.
mathematical_assessment.radius: For every global W-minimizer w, W(w)<=W(z) and f(z)<=f(w) imply delta/2*norm(w-x0)²<=delta/2*norm(z-x0)². Cancel delta>0 and use nonnegative norms to obtain norm(w-x0)<=norm(z-x0)<=R. This is stronger than membership in the construction ball and is not a convexity argument.
mathematical_assessment.transfer: For every x with W(x)<=W(w)+epsilon/2, nonnegative penalty and W(w)<=W(z) give f(x)-f(z)<=delta/2*norm(z-x0)²+epsilon/2<=epsilon. Retain actual W and actual supplied approximate point in the statement; no assumed f-error or surrogate quadratic-growth property.
mathematical_assessment.uniqueness: Not guaranteed without convexity/strict convexity; quantify an attained minimizer and possibly make the radius/transfer fact universal over minimizers. Do not claim a unique proximal map.
mathematical_assessment.properness: Closed-ball compactness is the load-bearing existence hypothesis. Proper Euclidean finite-dimensional normed spaces specialize correctly. Mere completeness of an arbitrary infinite-dimensional Hilbert space does not justify this compact-ball proof for a general continuous nonconvex f. Properness is a sufficient contract, not asserted necessary.
mathematical_assessment.zero_domains: R0 makes delta=epsilon/R² invalid under ordinary arithmetic; initial x0=z is already solved but outside this declaration. epsilon0 similarly defeats positive regularization and approximate tolerance. A positive upper R may still be supplied when x0=z, and then the theorem is valid.

smallest_substantive_statement: One theorem constructs a genuine global minimizer w of W at delta=epsilon/R², proves norm(w-x0)<=norm(z-x0), and proves every epsilon/2-approximate minimizer of this actual W transfers to f-error<=epsilon. This is a reusable existence-plus-comparison integration edge, materially beyond a conditional algebra-only wrapper; no gradient/smoothness/cost theorem required in this SAU.
proof_route: Define delta and W; prove delta>0 and W continuity.
Apply compact-ball extreme value theorem with known point z in the ball.
Compare every outside point against z using f global minimality and increasing positive quadratic penalty, obtaining global W minimality of the constructed point.
Compare W at the constructed minimizer and z, subtract f minimality and cancel positive delta to prove the sharper actual-radius bound.
For any supplied W-approximate point, discard its nonnegative penalty, compare Wmin to W(z), and substitute delta R²=epsilon to obtain f-error<=epsilon.
focused_consumers: Shifted scalar quadratic with center different from its original minimizer; verify an actual regularized minimizer lies strictly between them and exercise approximation transfer.
A continuous nonsmooth objective such as f(x)=abs x with x0=2,R2,epsilon4 (delta1) validates that no hidden C1/C2 premise is needed; w1 is an actual regularized minimizer.
Use a loose upper radius as well as the exact original distance to verify only a radius bound is assumed.
Case x0=z with positive R confirms proper nonzero denominator and valid zero original-distance comparison, without claiming literal R0 support.
